messages:
Carina: heads up — new latency dashboard p99 looks way higher for a subset of endpoints after the routing-policy rollout. p50/p95 fine though. anyone else see this?
Toni: I saw that too. which endpoints? can you paste the dashboard link? :eyes:
Carina: /app/console/dash/latency?view=by-route — look at routes that hit the fallback pool (weight 0.1 -> fallback). p99 jumps ~400ms on fallback routes. p95 unchanged.
Jasper: curious — p99 jumps but p95 stable often means a few long outliers. could be retries or a tag mismatch. do we still dedupe retry spans?
Kim: quick check: telemetry shows two route tags for those requests: `route=api.user.v1` and `route_fallback=api.user.v1-fallback`. some rollouts added `route_fallback` as a second tag instead of replacing `route`. that will split sample counts and can skew percentile merges.
Carina: ah that would explain why endpoint-level rollups move around depending on merge mode. p99 is sensitive to low-count buckets.
Toni: can you run the raw query for one endpoint and include sample_count? e.g. `SELECT percentile(duration_ms, 0.99), count() FROM requests WHERE route='api.user.v1' OR route_fallback='api.user.v1-fallback'` — we should see if counts are small.
Jasper: ran quick adhoc — for the fallback tag set count=37 in last 5m and the main tag count=1200. p99 for fallback group is 2.3s, main group 120ms. when we merge by summing weights naively the overall p99 moves toward the extreme 2.3s because we treated the small group as a separate cohort.
Carina: so the bug is effectively a provenance/sampling split: UI merges percentiles across origin tags without exposing sample counts -> misleading p99.
Kim: long term fix is to normalize route tags at ingestion (keep single canonical route) or change rollout to atomically switch the route tag. short term: console should surface sample_count and an origin badge for percentiles.
Toni: agree on two fixes. another short-term mitigation: compute percentiles from merged raw distributions (tdigest merge with weights) on the backend instead of merging per-cohort percentiles. that needs compute but gives correct p99.
Jasper: note: we already store tdigest blobs per shard for each tag. merge is doable if we bring blobs for both tags. current rollup job only stores merged percentiles, not blobs for transient tags.
Kim: ops question — is changing the rollout tagging backwards compatible with Dedicated customers that rely on route tag for billing/quota? need to check.
Carina: good point. we must not break quota attribution. maybe add `canonical_route` metadata and keep `route` for billing, but console uses canonical for metrics.
Toni: can we also add a warning on the latency card when sample_count < 100 or when there are multiple route origins contributing? UI should show a tooltip: "low sample count; percentiles may be unstable".
Jasper: +1. also provide a toggle: "compute from raw distribution" (slow) vs "use pre-merged percentiles" (fast). ops can leave default fast.
infra-bot: deploybot: Canary rollout of routing-policy v2 completed in prod region 3 at 2026-03-21T08:12:14Z :white_check_mark:
Kim: thanks infra-bot. after canary we saw the split appear. sounds like rollout left both tags live during a transition window.
Carina: next steps I propose: 1) patch console to show sample_count & origin badge (short PR) 2) add tooltip + low-sample warning 3) backend task to surface tdigest blobs for transient tags and compute merged percentile on-demand 4) product/solutions design to decide canonical tagging for billing/quota.
Toni: I'll open a tiny UI PR for sample_count + tooltip and a follow-up for toggle.
Jasper: I'll spike the tdigest-on-demand merge this afternoon and post perf numbers.
Kim: I'll coordinate with billing team about canonical route implications.
Carina: awesome — please drop updates here. thanks all :thumbsup:
Toni: filed https://redwood-internal/issue/ENGPLAT-7421 with UI mock and acceptance criteria.
Jasper: spike notes: pasted result of tdigest merge test — merged p99 stabilizes to 160ms versus naive merge 2.1s. CPU cost ~12% for query across 2 shards. will measure at scale.
Kim: keeping an eye. if we need an emergency dashboard patch, we can revert the rollout in region 3 or add a console-side hide for fallback routes.
Carina: prefer console patch first. avoid rolling back infra if not necessary.
infra-bot: alert: latency-card-variance-rule triggered for dashboard "Fallback routes — p99" (threshold 300ms) at 2026-03-21T08:18:02Z :rotating_light:
Carina: got the alert. I'll post a short blameless note and link the ticket. will follow up once PRs land.
Kim: FYI, clients using Dedicated may see quota attribution unchanged; we'll make console mapping non-destructive.
Toni: closing loop — UI PR up at https://redwood-internal/pull/1553, includes sample_count column and origin badge. requests review.
Jasper: spike branch at https://redwood-internal/git/tdigest-spike, added benchmarks. will attach numbers to ENGPLAT-7421.
Carina: thanks — nice triage.
